claims.text: The baseline composite contains 67.5 wt.% CoCrFeNiMo0.2, 12.5 wt.% Ni-coated MoS2, 15 wt.% Ag, and 5 wt.% Cr2O3 and is processed by spark plasma sintering.
The SPS process uses vacuum, 40 MPa pressure, heating to 1250 °C at 150 °C/min, a 3-minute hold, and furnace cooling.
Increasing x from 0.2 to 1 in CoCrFeNiMox increases FCC lattice distortion.
Increasing x from 0.2 to 1 promotes formation of a Mo-rich tetragonal σ phase.
High-temperature oxidation and tribochemical reactions produce a dense, continuous glaze containing silver molybdates and other oxides.
The σ phase acts as a reinforcing second phase that suppresses plastic deformation.
At lower temperatures, Ni/MoS2 and Ag jointly facilitate formation of a low-shear lubricating film.
At 600–800 °C, the oxide/molybdate glaze separates the sliding surfaces and reduces friction and material removal.
The Mo1 composite will have lower coefficient of friction and wear rate than the Mo0.2 composite throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The Mo1 composite will have greater hardness than the Mo0.2 baseline.
The Mo1 composite will exhibit better wear resistance than the Mo0.2 baseline, particularly at 800 °C.
The Mo1 coefficient of friction may not be lower than that of Mo0.2 at 200–400 °C.
The Mo0.2 baseline has a predominantly FCC solid-solution structure with minimal σ phase.
The Mo0.2 baseline has a friction coefficient of 0.66 at room temperature.
The Mo0.2 baseline reaches a friction coefficient of 0.75 at 200 °C and approximately 0.21 at 800 °C.
The Mo0.2 baseline wear rate is 13.1 × 10^-6 mm³/N·m at room temperature and 98.1 × 10^-6 mm³/N·m at 400 °C.
Competing thermal softening and wear-track roughening govern the uncertain friction behavior at 200–400 °C.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis predicts reduced coefficient of friction throughout the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range, whereas the predicted outcome concedes that friction may not be lower than the baseline at 200–400 °C.
